strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three generative tasks with consistent improvements and appropriate baseline selection

weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Fourier Knowledge Attention is a straightforward weighted combination of low-rank modules; blank infilling framework is directly borrowed from GLM [27]; patching and normalization from prior work. Each component is incremental.

Unclear technical details: Fourier attention mechanism lacks rigor (dimensions of K_f, definition of d_fk, initialization of A_i/B_i matrices unexplained); time granularity representation as a 5-tuple is rigid and dataset-specific.

Modest empirical improvements without statistical testing: 21/50 forecasting wins (42%), 1-3% gains on many datasets, no confidence intervals or significance tests provided. Mixed results on some tasks (second-best on Electricity imputation, worse than UP2ME on PSM anomaly detection).

Unfair experimental comparisons: different models use different pre-training datasets/strategies; unclear if GTM benefits from more/better data or the method itself. Pre-training gains (0.5-11%) may not justify complexity.

Reproducibility concerns: incomplete UTSD-12G preprocessing details, arbitrary low-rank dimensions (385×1), no code availability, missing fine-tuning protocols and hyperparameter selection procedures.
Loose terminology and presentation: 'universal knowledge,' 'knowledge attention' used imprecisely; Figure 2 overly complex; key technical details relegated to appendix rather than main paper.

Limited analysis of time granularity effectiveness: no visualization of learned attention weights, no analysis of when/why granularity matters, no evaluation on unknown/misspecified granularities at inference time.
